content.user_title: Explain Robotics, ROS 2, and Physical AI
content.value_statement: Robotics learners and builders need clear guidance across ROS 2, simulation, perception, and control. This skill provides concise explanations, project guidance, and troubleshooting support for Physical AI work.
actual_capabilities: Explains ROS 2 Humble concepts and middleware roles.
Summarizes Isaac Sim and Gazebo simulation choices.
Clarifies inverse kinematics, SLAM, reinforcement learning, and computer vision concepts.
Outlines modules, labs, and capstone project structure.
Provides ROS 2 Python and C++ example guidance for robotics tasks.
Helps troubleshoot simulation issues at a conceptual level.
limitations: Does not include full lab files or runnable simulator assets.
Cannot validate robot hardware safety or real-world deployment readiness.
Focuses on ROS 2 Humble and listed robotics topics.
Requires user-provided project details for specific debugging advice.

use_cases.title: Learn Core Robotics Concepts
use_cases.description: Get clear explanations of ROS 2, SLAM, inverse kinematics, perception, and reinforcement learning.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot Simulation Workflows
use_cases.description: Reason through Gazebo or Isaac Sim setup issues and connect them to ROS 2 design choices.

use_cases.title: Plan Physical AI Curriculum
use_cases.description: Organize modules, labs, and capstone activities around embodied intelligence and robot systems.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Robotics Topic
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain ROS 2 Humble to a beginner. Cover nodes, topics, services, and why middleware matters in robotics.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Simulators
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Isaac Sim and Gazebo for my robotics project. Include strengths, tradeoffs, and when each simulator fits best.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Lab Exercise
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a hands-on ROS 2 lab for week one. Include learning goals, required setup, tasks, and expected outcomes.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Capstone Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my humanoid robotics capstone architecture. Evaluate perception, control, simulation, and sim-to-real risks.

output_examples.input: Explain SLAM for a robotics student.
output_examples.output: SLAM lets a robot build a map while estimating its own position. The explanation would cover sensors, landmarks, motion uncertainty, and mapping tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: Help plan a ROS 2 simulation lab.
output_examples.output: A useful response would define objectives, simulator setup, ROS 2 communication goals, validation steps, and common troubleshooting checks.

output_examples.input: Assess a humanoid robot capstone idea.
output_examples.output: The skill would review perception, balance, control loops, simulation scope, data needs, and risks before hardware testing.

best_practices: Provide the robot type, simulator, ROS 2 version, and current failure mode.
Ask for concept explanations before requesting implementation details.
Separate simulation questions from real hardware safety decisions.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for hardware deployment advice without safety constraints.
Do not expect complete runnable projects from brief topic prompts.
Do not mix unrelated simulator, perception, and control issues in one vague request.

faq.question: What robotics topics does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Physical AI, ROS 2 Humble, simulation, inverse kinematics, SLAM, reinforcement learning, and computer vision.

faq.question: Can it help with ROS 2 code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can explain ROS 2 patterns and provide Python or C++ example guidance.

faq.question: Does it run Gazebo or Isaac Sim?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and troubleshooting support, but it does not run simulators itself.

faq.question: Is it useful for humanoid robotics?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes humanoid robotics concepts and can review perception, control, and simulation plans.

faq.question: Can instructors use it for course planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help organize modules, lab exercises, and capstone project outlines.

faq.question: Does it replace hardware safety review?
faq.answer: No. Real robot deployment needs qualified safety review, testing procedures, and hardware-specific validation.
